layout.explanation: Choose layout to automatically place named boxes and route directed edges. Use this for dependency/lineage graphs and feedback flows; it produces SVG, editable DOT, raw plain geometry and inspected JSON.

fields.explanation: Declare a directed dependency or flow graph for automatic native layout. Nodes and directed edges are required; geometry is generated, never authored. This document publishes SVG, editable DOT and checked layout geometry.

/properties/version.explanation: Select the graph input contract schemaxis.graphviz/1. This is the document language version; native Graphviz 16.1.0 qualification is recorded separately.

/properties/operation.explanation: Choose layout to automatically place named boxes and route directed edges. Use this for dependency/lineage graphs and feedback flows; it produces SVG, editable DOT, raw plain geometry and inspected JSON.

/properties/nodes.explanation: List every named task or entity, including disconnected ones, in stable presentation order. Supply 2–200 nodes with unique IDs. Labels are visible text; edge identity always uses IDs.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: Describe one graph entity with a stable unitless ID and short visible label. Every entity becomes a fixed 2.5 by 0.5 inch box; no authored coordinates or native attributes are accepted.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/id.explanation: Give this node a distinct lowercase ASCII identifier, beginning with a letter, followed by letters/digits/underscores, at most 32 characters. For example build is referenced by edge source/target; changing the label never changes this identity.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/label.explanation: Set literal visible text of 1–24 ASCII characters. Start with a letter/digit and use letters/digits/spaces or ._:/()+-. For example Extract 01 or version 2. Quotes, backslashes, HTML and escapes fail; numeric labels must remain strings. Font rendering is not measured.

/properties/edges.explanation: Declare 1–500 unique directed dependencies using node IDs. A source precedes a target in DAG mode. Duplicate pairs, self-edges and unknown endpoints fail; reversing a pair reverses the dependency.

/properties/edges/items.explanation: Describe one directed dependency between two distinct declared nodes. This creates a routed cubic spline and normal arrowhead pointing toward target. There are no ports, labels or arbitrary attributes.

/properties/edges/items/properties/sourc.explanation: Name the tail node ID, such as extract. This is a unitless reference to a declared ID, never a label, path or URL. In DAG mode it lies above or left of target according to rankDirection.

/properties/edges/items/properties/targe.explanation: Name the arrowhead node ID, such as build. The target must exist and differ from source. A feedback edge needs explicit cyclic policy because it can violate dependency order.

/properties/rankDirection.explanation: Choose TB to lay DAG dependencies from top to bottom, or LR from left to right. Omission uses TB. This changes layout orientation without changing topology; coordinates remain inches from lower left, and SVG uses inverted y.

/properties/graphPolicy.explanation: Choose dag for acyclic dependencies; omission uses dag and any cycle fails before native launch. Choose cyclic explicitly for feedback flows. Cyclic graphs preserve topology but do not promise every edge moves forward through ranks.
